title: William the Silent is assassinated in Delft
summary: Balthasar Gerard, a Catholic supporter of Philip II, shot William of Orange, leader of the Dutch Revolt, at his residence in Delft.
reason: Philip II had declared William an outlaw and promised a reward to anyone who killed him.
significance: It was one of the first assassinations of a head of state with a handgun, and the revolt continued under his son Maurice.
